Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level. The numbers are said the way a teacher tells what happened ('pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a state report (S2-09). The term is not named before the example by any teaching beat of the same concept either (a sister part may not explain 'the UPI route' before the ₹100 kirana payment runs; a hook or a question to the student may ask about it): BIE's code sends such a script back.
[S2-09] Complete teacher sentences (Navin's verdict on Money v1, 29 October 2026: 'teacher ki naration uske sentence aise poore ho ki banawati na lage aur cheejen samjhane ki process us par depend hai to unka complete tarike se istemal hona jaruri hai'): the narration tells what happened in full, natural sentences; a story's numbers are said conversationally ('pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a ledger's state report ('cash ₹500 से ₹400 हुआ', 'savings ₹0 से ₹500 हुईं'). BIE's code sends such a beat back.
[S2-10] Outside facts carry their dated source (the Money lesson resume -d, 29 October 2026, v10: operational descriptions of UPI, NEFT, RTGS and IMPS added real Indian banking knowledge beyond the book without a dated source): for a competitive-exam learner (level upsc_pcs), a teaching beat whose basis is outside the book, or mixed and naming an institution or system that none of its book lines names, carries its source with its year in `source` ('RBI, NEFT FAQ, 2023'); a story, example, hook, analogy or question needs none; a beat whose facts the book line says has basis 'book'. BIE's code sends such a beat back; the review page lists the outside beats with their sources.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-29.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Video v12: NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI—और AePS, BBPS
Goal: Learner settlement, availability, limits और charges की दिशा पर payment systems की comparison करेगा; AePS की inclusion भूमिका और BBPS के bill-payment काम को अलग पहचान सकेगा।
Opening hook: बड़ी रकम भेजनी हो, तुरंत छोटा payment करना हो या bill भरना हो—क्या हर जरूरत के लिए वही system चुनेंगे?
Story or analogy: पहले अलग payment needs आएँगी, फिर एक criterion पर सभी relevant systems साथ रखेंगे। Settlement का तरीका, operating hours, amount limits और inward–outward charges को अलग rows में पढ़ेंगे; AePS और BBPS को उनके काम की situations से पहचानेंगे।
Planned minutes: 8
Narration time (S2-01): 7.1-9.5 minutes, about 923-1235 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

Items (item id | page | kind | type | content), each with its teacher questions (question id | ask | question → answer | basis) and its unpack from Section 1 (term | why | example | consequence | visual), plus any locked explanation (Navin's verdict: speak it) and any locked narration (Navin locked these spoken lines: keep them word for word in the beats that cover the item):
p014-i3 | 14 | list_point | facts_numbers | • Available 24×7. Free of cost
  p014-i3#q1 | what | What availability and cost does the page attribute to NEFT? → It describes NEFT as available throughout the day and week and free of cost. | book
  p014-i3#q2 | evidence | What other part of the page supports the availability statement? → The comparison table also lists NEFT availability as 24×7, all days. | book
  p014-i3#q3 | why | Why should availability not be confused with immediate settlement? → A system can accept instructions at any hour but still settle them in batches; operating hours and settlement method answer different questions. | outside
  term | 24×7 | yaani दिन के 24 घंटे, हफ्ते के सातों दिन उपलब्ध | image: रविवार रात को भी transfer का विकल्प खुला है
  why | A payment need can arise outside bank-branch hours. [standard] → NEFT is available 24×7, but its separate batch rule still governs settlement. [book]
  example or place | A customer using banking services on a weekend.
  consequence | Read timing, speed and charges as separate attributes.
  visual | Keep the clock running while a batch queue forms.
  level extra | Do not extend the page's fee statement into an independently verified rule for every channel.
p014-i4 | 14 | list_point | process | • Transfers occur in half-hourly batches.
  p014-i4#q1 | how | How are NEFT transfers processed according to this page? → Transfers are grouped into batches rather than each being settled immediately on its own. | book
  p014-i4#q2 | when | When do these batches occur? → The page specifies half-hourly batches. | book
  p014-i4#q3 | why | Why can a customer face some waiting despite 24×7 availability? → An instruction submitted between processing rounds may wait for a subsequent batch; continuous availability does not remove the batching interval. | outside
  p014-i4#q4 | how | How does the hypothetical example distinguish batch processing from a credit deadline? → Instructions submitted at different times join one illustrated processing round. That round's time identifies when the group is processed, not a promise that each recipient's account is credited at that exact moment. | outside
  term | batches | yaani कई transfer को एक समूह में लेकर निपटाना | image: अलग-अलग चिट्ठियाँ इकट्ठी करके एक साथ डाक की थैली भेजना
  why | Many customers submit transfer instructions at different times. [standard] → NEFT groups transfers into half-hourly batches, so submission and settlement need not coincide. [book]
  example or place | A hypothetical Jaipur neighbourhood: Meena pays rent, Ravi pays a flour supplier, and Saira pays a school fee through NEFT.
  consequence | Round-the-clock access does not mean each instruction is processed immediately or credited at a guaranteed batch timestamp.
  visual | Queue three time-stamped instructions, group them, and release the batch before showing completed credits.
  level extra | The times illustrate grouping only: eligibility for a particular batch and beneficiary-credit timing are not guaranteed by this example.
  real world (run it first, with these numbers, then name the term) | place: Hypothetical Jaipur neighbourhood and its bank accounts | actors: Meena, a tenant, Mr Sharma, her landlord, Ravi, a kirana shopkeeper, Asha Flour Suppliers, Saira, a parent, Uday School, the customers' banks | goods: ₹2000 rent, ₹3000 payment for flour, ₹1000 school fee | numbers: instructions waiting in the illustrated group 0 at 10:00 → 3 by 10:22; Meena's illustrative balance after successful transfer, ignoring charges ₹10000 → ₹8000; Mr Sharma's illustrative balance after credit ₹1000 → ₹3000
    step 1 | Assume an illustrated processing round has finished at 10:00. Meena submits ₹2000 rent at 10:05, Ravi submits ₹3000 for flour at 10:12, and Saira submits ₹1000 school fees at 10:22. | shows: Separate payment needs generate multiple instructions at different submission times.
    step 2 | Assume all three instructions are eligible for the illustrated 10:30 round. They join one batch totalling ₹6000 rather than each being processed immediately when submitted. | shows: Half-hourly batch processing groups instructions for a subsequent processing round.
    step 3 | After Meena's transfer completes and the beneficiary credit is posted, her balance is ₹8000 and Mr Sharma's is ₹3000. The example does not assert that this credit occurs exactly at 10:30. | shows: Batch processing leads onward to beneficiary credit, but the processing timestamp is not itself a guaranteed credit deadline.
    then the name | This grouping of separate instructions into a half-hourly processing round illustrates NEFT batching.
    real life | The page identifies NEFT with regular bank transfers; rent, supplier payments and school fees are hypothetical applications of that use.
p014-i5 | 14 | list_point | facts_numbers | • Suitable for ordinary bank transfers.
  p014-i5#q1 | what | What kind of use does the page associate with NEFT? → It associates NEFT with ordinary or regular bank transfers rather than specifically urgent high-value transfers. | book
  p014-i5#q2 | evidence | Where is this use repeated in the graphic? → The Primary Use row calls NEFT's use 'Regular bank transfers'. | book
  p014-i5#q3 | why | Why can batching be acceptable for an ordinary transfer? → When immediate completion is not essential, a short processing wait may be compatible with the payer's purpose. | outside
  term | ordinary bank transfers | yaani रोज़मर्रा में एक account से दूसरे account में पैसे भेजना | image: घर का खर्च दूसरे शहर में भेजना
  why | Many payments do not require immediate settlement. [standard] → The page presents NEFT as suitable for regular transfers and RTGS for high-value urgent transfers. [book]
  example or place | A routine household bank transfer.
  consequence | Choose a service by urgency as well as amount.
  visual | Sort routine and urgent payment cards.
  level extra | 'Suitable for' is not an exclusive legal restriction.
p014-i6 | 14 | list_point | facts_numbers | • Mainly for small amounts upto 5 lakh (Limit varies from bank to bank)
  p014-i6#q1 | what | What amount description and qualification appear in the NEFT prose? → It says NEFT is mainly for small amounts upto 5 lakh and adds that the limit varies from bank to bank. | book
  p014-i6#q2 | evidence | What prevents reading ₹5 lakh as an unqualified system-wide NEFT maximum? → The prose itself qualifies the limit by bank, while the table states 'No fixed limit' for NEFT's maximum amount. | book
  p014-i6#q3 | why | Why distinguish a bank's limit from a payment system's limit? → A bank or access channel may restrict what its customer can initiate without that restriction defining the underlying system's universal ceiling. | outside
  term | Limit varies from bank to bank | yaani हर bank की भेजने की सीमा एक जैसी होना ज़रूरी नहीं | image: दो banking apps पर अलग transfer limits दिखना
  why | A customer needs to know whether a proposed payment is permitted. [standard] → The page's bank-specific qualification must be read alongside the table's absence of a fixed NEFT maximum. [book]
  example or place | The transfer-limit setting in a bank's app.
  consequence | Separate typical usage, bank limits and system limits.
  visual | Place bank-specific limit cards beneath the broader system.
  level extra | A likely statement trap is replacing 'mainly' with 'only'.
p014-i8 | 14 | table_row | comparison | Full Form | NEFT: National Electronic Funds Transfer | RTGS: Real-Time Gross Settlement | IMPS: Immediate Payment Service | UPI: Unified Payments Interface
  p014-i8#q1 | compare | What do the four abbreviations expand to? → NEFT expands to National Electronic Funds Transfer; RTGS to Real-Time Gross Settlement; IMPS to Immediate Payment Service; and UPI to Unified Payments Interface. | book
  p014-i8#q2 | difference | Which names emphasise settlement, immediacy and an interface respectively? → RTGS names gross settlement, IMPS names immediate payment, and UPI names a payments interface; NEFT names electronic funds transfer. | book
  p014-i8#q3 | how | How can the names help without substituting for the comparison? → They provide cues, but timing, minimum amounts and operating institutions still need separate checking; a name does not specify every service condition. | outside
  term | Interface | yaani वह जुड़ने का तरीका जिससे payment की सुविधा इस्तेमाल होती है | image: फोन की screen से bank payment शुरू करना
  why | Similar payment abbreviations can be confused. [standard] → Expanding the names supplies an initial cue, then the table separates their actual features. [standard]
  example or place | Payment choices displayed in banking and payment applications.
  consequence | Attach each acronym to its correct feature set.
  visual | Expand each acronym into its full name.
  level extra | Do not assume that UPI is itself a bank from the word 'Interface'.
p014-i9 | 14 | table_row | comparison | Regulator | NEFT: RBI | RTGS: RBI | IMPS: NPCI | UPI: NPCI
  p014-i9#q1 | compare | How does the printed Regulator row group the systems? → It groups NEFT and RTGS under RBI and IMPS and UPI under NPCI. | book
  p014-i9#q2 | difference | What institutional distinction needs care when teaching this row? → The table uses 'Regulator' broadly: NPCI operates payment systems, whereas RBI has the overarching regulatory role. Operator and regulator should not be treated as interchangeable institutional functions. | outside
  p014-i9#q3 | why | Why is this distinction important? → The organisation running the network and the authority overseeing payment systems perform different roles, even when a simplified comparison places them in the same row. | outside
  term | RBI | yaani भारत का central bank, जो banks और payments की व्यवस्था की निगरानी करता है | image: कई banks के ऊपर निगरानी की एक छत
  term | NPCI | yaani National Payments Corporation of India, जो कई retail payment systems चलाता है | image: अलग banks को जोड़ने वाला payment network
  why | A payment service needs an organisation to run it and a framework for oversight. [standard] → Distinguishing these roles prevents the printed grouping from becoming a misleading equivalence. [standard]
  example or place | RBI-associated NEFT/RTGS versus NPCI-associated IMPS/UPI in the table.
  consequence | Match services to institutions without confusing operation with regulation.
  visual | Group the services, then separate operator and oversight labels.
  level extra | NPCI's expansion and the role clarification are outside explanations.
p014-i10 | 14 | table_row | comparison | Settlement Type | NEFT: Batch-based (half-hourly) | RTGS: Real-time, gross settlement | IMPS: Real-time | UPI: Real-time
  p014-i10#q1 | compare | How do settlement types differ in the table? → NEFT is batch-based at half-hourly intervals; RTGS is described as real-time gross settlement; IMPS and UPI are labelled real-time. | book
  p014-i10#q2 | difference | What does 'gross' add beyond 'real-time'? → Real-time concerns when processing occurs; gross means an individual transaction is settled separately rather than being reduced to a net amount against other transactions. | outside
  p014-i10#q3 | how | How should the simplified IMPS and UPI cells be interpreted? → They communicate immediate transfer behaviour for the user; the table does not explain the separate interbank settlement arrangements of these systems. | outside
  term | gross settlement | yaani हर transfer को अलग पूरा निपटाना, दूसरे transfers से काटकर सिर्फ बची रकम नहीं | image: हर bill अलग पूरा चुकाना, हिसाब जोड़कर सिर्फ अंतर नहीं देना
  term | real-time | yaani instruction आने पर उसी समय processing होना | image: बिना अगली खेप का इंतज़ार किए payment आगे बढ़ना
  why | A payer needs to know both waiting time and how transactions are settled. [standard] → Batch versus real-time concerns timing; gross concerns treatment of individual transactions. [standard]
  example or place | Comparing a routine NEFT instruction with a high-value RTGS payment.
  consequence | Timing and settlement basis become two separate comparison axes.
  visual | Queue NEFT instructions and release RTGS transactions individually.
  level extra | The IMPS and UPI labels should not be expanded into unsupported claims about interbank settlement.
p014-i11 | 14 | table_row | comparison | Availability | NEFT: 24×7, all days | RTGS: 24×7, all days | IMPS: 24×7, all days | UPI: 24×7, all days
  p014-i11#q1 | compare | How do the four services compare in stated availability? → The table gives the same availability for each: 24×7 on all days. | book
  p014-i11#q2 | difference | Does this row distinguish any one service from the other three? → No; availability is shared here, while settlement type and limits distinguish them elsewhere in the table. | book
  p014-i11#q3 | why | Why is 24×7 availability not a promise that no transaction will fail or be delayed? → Availability describes the service schedule; an individual transfer still depends on connectivity, bank systems and transaction conditions. | outside
  term | Availability | yaani किस समय service इस्तेमाल के लिए खुली है | image: branch बंद है, पर phone में transfer का विकल्प खुला है
  why | Payment needs can arise on holidays or at night. [standard] → All four services are listed as available throughout those periods. [book]
  example or place | A Sunday payment through an electronic banking channel.
  consequence | Use other rows, not availability alone, to choose among services.
  visual | Run one seven-day clock across all four columns.
  level extra | Shared availability is compatible with different processing speeds.
p014-i12 | 14 | table_row | comparison | Speed | NEFT: Slower (batch processing) | RTGS: Instant for high-value | IMPS: Instant | UPI: Instant
  p014-i12#q1 | compare | How does the table compare transfer speed? → NEFT is labelled slower because of batch processing, RTGS instant for high-value transfers, and IMPS and UPI instant. | book
  p014-i12#q2 | difference | Which service has the distinct waiting structure in this row? → NEFT is the one associated with batches rather than instant transfer in the table. | book
  p014-i12#q3 | why | Why does batching affect speed? → An instruction may have to wait for the next processing round rather than proceed separately on arrival. | outside
  term | Instant | yaani सामान्य रूप से तुरंत transfer होना | image: भेजने के बाद दूसरे phone पर payment की सूचना आना
  why | An urgent payer wants to avoid waiting for a processing round. [standard] → The table contrasts NEFT batching with the instant descriptions of the other three services. [book]
  example or place | An urgent payment contrasted with a routine transfer.
  consequence | Speed matters independently of the amount permitted.
  visual | Hold one payment at a batch gate while the others pass.
  level extra | 'Instant' is the printed service description, not an unconditional guarantee against operational delay.
p014-i13 | 14 | table_row | comparison | Minimum Amount | NEFT: No minimum | RTGS: 2 lakh | IMPS: No minimum | UPI: No minimum
  p014-i13#q1 | compare | How do the minimum amounts compare? → The table gives RTGS a minimum of 2 lakh and says no minimum for NEFT, IMPS and UPI. | book
  p014-i13#q2 | difference | Which service is singled out by an explicit lower threshold? → RTGS is singled out by its ₹2 lakh minimum, consistent with the page's high-value emphasis. | book
  p014-i13#q3 | how | How can the threshold be used in an illustrative choice? → A ₹50000 transfer falls below the printed RTGS threshold, whereas ₹200000 reaches it; other conditions still need checking. | outside
  term | Minimum Amount | yaani कम से कम कितने पैसे का transfer किया जा सकता है | image: दरवाज़े पर लिखा हो: ₹2 lakh से entry शुरू
  why | A payer must first check whether an amount meets a service's entry threshold. [standard] → The table gives RTGS an explicit threshold unlike the other columns. [book]
  example or place | Checking whether a proposed bank payment qualifies for RTGS.
  consequence | A high maximum does not remove a minimum requirement.

beats.say: किराया भेजना हो, supplier को बड़ी रकम तुरंत देनी हो, या बिजली का bill भरना हो—क्या हर जरूरत का रास्ता एक होगा? पहले payment होते देखिए, फिर सही system चुनेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Rent, supplier payment and electricity bill cards.

beats.say: Jaipur में Meena को ₹2000 किराया भेजना है। उनके पास ₹10000 हैं; transfer पूरा होने पर ₹8000 बचेंगे। मकान मालिक के पास पहले ₹1000 थे; पैसे मिलने पर ₹3000 होंगे। पर बीच में processing कैसे होगी?
beats.on_screen: Meena and landlord accounts; completed-credit outcome shown separately from processing.

beats.say: मानिए 10:00 का processing round खत्म हुआ। Meena ने 10:05 पर ₹2000, Ravi ने 10:12 पर आटे के ₹3000, और Saira ने 10:22 पर school fee के ₹1000 भेजने को कहा।
beats.on_screen: Three instructions appear in timestamp order.

beats.say: मानिए तीनों instructions अगले 10:30 round के लिए eligible हैं। अब ₹6000 के 3 instructions साथ process होंगे। यह NEFT batching है: transfers को समूह में लेकर हर आधे घंटे process करना; 10:30 हर account में credit की guarantee नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Three instructions enter one half-hourly batch; credit appears downstream without a promised timestamp.
beats.source: RBI, NEFT Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: अब Kavita को steel के ₹300000 Arjun को तुरंत देने हैं। उनके Bank A में ₹500000 हैं; Arjun के Bank B में ₹100000 हैं। मानिए instruction सही है और bank के पास settlement के लिए पर्याप्त पैसे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Separate customer balances and bank settlement accounts.

beats.say: RBI में Bank A के settlement account से पूरे ₹300000 Bank B को मिलते हैं, बिना दूसरा payment आने का इंतजार किए। Customer credit पूरा होने पर Kavita के ₹200000 बचते हैं और Arjun के पास ₹400000 हो जाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Full ₹300000 settlement arrow; customer ledgers update separately.

beats.say: बाद में Arjun पुराने cancelled order के ₹200000 वापस भेजते हैं। यह रकम अलग पूरी settle होती है; Arjun के ₹200000 बचते हैं और Kavita के ₹400000 होते हैं। दोनों payments को काटकर सिर्फ ₹100000 नहीं भेजे गए।
beats.on_screen: Separate reverse ₹200000 arrow; do not replace arrows with ₹100000 net.

beats.say: यह RTGS है: real-time यानी batch का इंतजार नहीं; gross यानी हर transaction की पूरी रकम अलग settle होती है। यह 24×7 उपलब्ध है। बड़ी urgent payment में इसी अलग, तुरंत processing की जरूरत होती है।
beats.on_screen: Real-time = timing; gross = individual full value; 24×7.
beats.source: RBI, RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: Instruction गलत हो या जरूरी funds न हों, तो यह सफल run मान नहीं सकते। इसलिए instant को हर हालत में सफलता की guarantee मत बनाइए।
beats.on_screen: Validity and funds checks before settlement.
beats.source: RBI, RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: पूरा रास्ता देखिए: किराए वाले instructions समूह में अगले round तक पहुँचे; steel payment अपनी पूरी रकम के साथ अलग चला। Processing के बाद customer credit को अलग पहचानिए।
beats.on_screen: Replay both examples without repeating balances.
beats.source: RBI, NEFT and RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: याद रखिए: NEFT में half-hourly batches; RTGS में बिना batching, हर payment का पूरा अलग settlement। दोनों का खुला रहना और processing का तरीका अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: NEFT → batch; RTGS → individual full-value settlement.

beats.say: रविवार रात घर पैसे भेजने हों तो? NEFT 24×7 है, यानी दिन-रात, सातों दिन उपलब्ध; free of cost बताया जाता है। इसका सामान्य काम regular bank transfers है, जैसे घर का खर्च भेजना।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: all days; free-of-cost description; routine household transfer.

beats.say: Supplier की बड़ी payment में RTGS मुख्यतः high-value काम करता है और इसे RBI सीधे operate करता है। Sender से ₹50 तक fee लेने की अनुमति है; इसका मतलब हर बार ₹50 लेना जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: high-value; RBI operator; sender fee ceiling ₹50, not compulsory flat charge.

beats.say: रात में जरूरी पैसे भेजने हों तो IMPS immediate transfer देता है और round the clock उपलब्ध है। Bank के mobile और internet banking से इसे इस्तेमाल करते हैं; ATM भी इसका listed access रास्ता है।
beats.on_screen: IMPS: immediate; 24×7; mobile banking, internet banking, ATM.

beats.say: NEFT के लिए मुख्यतः ₹5 lakh तक, bank के हिसाब से बदलती limit वाला वर्णन मिलता है; fixed system maximum नहीं। IMPS का range ₹1 से ₹5 lakh लिखा मिलता है, जबकि minimum की दूसरी wording ‘No minimum’ है।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: typical-use description ≠ fixed ceiling. IMPS: ₹1–₹5 lakh; alternative minimum wording: No minimum; bank variation.

beats.say: इसलिए ‘मुख्यतः’ को ‘सिर्फ’ मत पढ़िए। RTGS की ₹2 lakh entry बड़ी रकम वाला उपयोग समझाती है; fee में sender और ‘तक’ याद रखिए। IMPS में speed, समय और access तीन अलग बातें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Typical use ≠ exclusive use; sender fee ≤ ₹50; speed ≠ schedule ≠ channel.

beats.say: Banking screen के इन 4 options में समान क्या है? सभी electronic payment के रास्ते हैं और चारों 24×7, all days उपलब्ध हैं। इसलिए सिर्फ रविवार को खुला होने से कोई एक नहीं चुन सकते।
beats.on_screen: Four columns share one seven-day clock.

beats.say: NEFT का पूरा नाम National Electronic Funds Transfer; RTGS का Real-Time Gross Settlement है। IMPS, Immediate Payment Service है; UPI, Unified Payments Interface है। Interface यानी payment इस्तेमाल करने का जुड़ने वाला रास्ता, जैसे phone की payment screen।
beats.on_screen: Expand all four acronyms; highlight Transfer, Settlement, Immediate and Interface.

beats.say: संस्था जोड़िए: NEFT और RTGS के साथ RBI; IMPS और UPI के साथ NPCI। लेकिन operator और regulator एक काम नहीं हैं: NPCI networks चलाता है, जबकि payments की ऊपर से regulatory निगरानी RBI की है।
beats.on_screen: Institution matching; separate operator and overarching regulator labels.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

beats.say: Settlement में NEFT half-hourly batch-based है; RTGS real-time gross है। IMPS और UPI real-time बताए जाते हैं। Speed में NEFT अपेक्षाकृत धीमा, RTGS high-value के लिए instant, और IMPS तथा UPI instant हैं।
beats.on_screen: Settlement and speed displayed as separate rows.

beats.say: Minimum में RTGS के लिए ₹2 lakh हैं; NEFT, IMPS और UPI के लिए ‘No minimum’ है। इसलिए ₹50000 RTGS की entry तक नहीं पहुँचते, ₹200000 पहुँचते हैं; यह minimum है, maximum नहीं।
beats.on_screen: ₹50000 below RTGS gate; ₹200000 meets gate; other columns: No minimum.

beats.say: Maximum में NEFT की fixed limit नहीं, RTGS की upper limit नहीं। IMPS ₹5 lakh है, bank के हिसाब से बदल सकता है। UPI में ₹1 lakh default और Person-to-Merchant के लिए ₹10 lakh वाला वर्णन मिलता है।
beats.on_screen: Four maximum cells; keep bank and eligible-category qualification tags attached.

beats.say: काम के हिसाब से NEFT regular transfer, RTGS बड़ी urgent payment, IMPS रोजमर्रा की urgent payment है। UPI mobile-based peer-to-peer, यानी दोस्त को पैसे, और merchant payment, यानी दुकान पर payment के लिए है।
beats.on_screen: Routine family transfer; urgent supplier payment; urgent everyday transfer; friend and shop payments.

beats.say: पहुँचने के रास्ते देखिए: NEFT और RTGS में internet तथा mobile banking; IMPS में इनके साथ ATMs भी हैं। UPI में GPay, PhonePe जैसे mobile apps हैं। Screen वाला रास्ता और पीछे का payment system अलग पहचानिए।
beats.on_screen: Channel icons connect to service columns; ATM highlighted under IMPS.

beats.say: NEFT में अगला round आने तक इंतजार हो सकता है, इसलिए 24×7 का मतलब instant नहीं। RTGS में gross रकम का तरीका बताता है, सिर्फ बड़ी रकम नहीं; IMPS और UPI का instant user experience अलग interbank हिसाब की पूरी कहानी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Availability ≠ speed; gross ≠ high-value; customer experience ≠ complete interbank settlement description.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

beats.say: Statement trap है: ‘हर merchant payment ₹10 lakh तक हो सकता है।’ गलत—बढ़ी UPI limit eligible category और लागू conditions पर निर्भर है; merchant QR भर काफी नहीं। इसी तरह bank की limit को पूरे system की limit मत बनाइए।
beats.on_screen: Reject universal ₹10 lakh merchant entitlement; require eligible category and conditions.
beats.source: NPCI, UPI, Enhancement of Transaction Limits for Certain Categories, 2025

beats.say: Comparison का क्रम रखिए: संस्था, settlement, समय, speed, minimum, maximum, काम और channel। सबसे जरूरी जोड़ी है availability बनाम speed; और सबसे जरूरी संख्या RTGS की ₹2 lakh minimum है।
beats.on_screen: Compact difference table retaining qualifications for every limit.

beats.say: गाँव में branch दूर हो, तो account के पैसे हाथ में कैसे आएँ? एक ग्राहक के खाते में ₹1000 हैं और उसे ₹500 निकालने हैं; पास के मदद वाले banking counter पर काम हो सकता है।
beats.on_screen: Village, distant branch and nearby assisted counter.

beats.say: ग्राहक Aadhaar और उँगली के निशान से पहचान जाँच करवाता है। सफल authorised withdrawal के बाद उसे ₹500 मिलते हैं और खाते में ₹500 बचते हैं; पहचान जाँचना और पैसे देना अलग कदम हैं।
beats.on_screen: Identity check, authorisation, cash handover and account debit in order.

beats.say: यह Aadhaar Enabled Payment System, AEPS का उदाहरण है। Biometrics यानी शरीर की पहचान से जाँच; Bank Mitras bank की सेवा पास पहुँचाने वाले लोग हैं। इनके जरिए authentication और payment होता है, जिससे banking से दूर व्यक्ति को पहुँच मिलती है।
beats.on_screen: AEPS: Aadhaar + biometrics → assisted banking through Bank Mitra.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: अगर पहचान की जाँच सफल नहीं होती, तो इस run में authorised withdrawal पूरा नहीं मानेंगे। सिर्फ Aadhaar बताना और सफल banking transaction होना एक बात नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Failed authentication stops the illustrated withdrawal path.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

beats.say: क्रम फिर देखिए: ग्राहक ने request दी, पहचान जाँची गई, अनुमति मिलने पर पैसे निकले। पास का counter दूरी की परेशानी घटाता है; पहचान की जाँच सुरक्षा वाला अलग काम करती है।
beats.on_screen: Request → authenticate → authorise → withdraw.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: AEPS को Aadhaar, biometrics और Bank Mitra से जोड़िए। इसका inclusion वाला काम है banking की पहुँच देना, सिर्फ phone से payment करवाना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Identity + assisted access → financial inclusion.

beats.say: खाते में सरकारी पैसा आ जाए, लेकिन व्यक्ति उसे इस्तेमाल न कर पाए, तो मदद कितनी काम आएगी? मानिए खाते में पहले ₹0 थे; सरकार के ₹500 आने पर अब ₹500 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government subsidy credits beneficiary account.

beats.say: अब वह व्यक्ति Bank Mitra के पास Aadhaar-biometric जाँच से इस पैसे तक पहुँचता है। यह AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को सहारा देना है: खाते में आई सरकारी मदद को इस्तेमाल करने का रास्ता मिलता है।
beats.on_screen: Credit first; local access second.

beats.say: पहली कड़ी है सरकार से account में benefit पहुँचना; दूसरी है व्यक्ति की banking तक पहुँच। दूर branch की रुकावट घटे तो पैसा इस्तेमाल हो सकेगा—यही grassroots तक मदद पहुँचाने का मतलब है।
beats.on_screen: Benefit delivery → account credit → accessible banking → usable benefit.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: सरकारी subsidies को grassroots तक पहुँचाने में AEPS की भूमिका इसी access में है। गाँव का counter account और व्यक्ति के बीच बची दूरी को कम करता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight access bridge between beneficiary and credited account.

beats.say: लेकिन Bank Mitra तक पहुँच होने से subsidy की eligibility तय नहीं होती। सरकारी benefit देना और बाद में उसकी banking access देना अलग भूमिकाएँ हैं।
beats.on_screen: Access channel ≠ subsidy eligibility decision.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: याद रखिए: पहले benefit खाते में, फिर उसे इस्तेमाल करने की पहुँच। AEPS इस दूसरी कड़ी को मजबूत करके Direct Benefits Transfer में मदद करता है।
beats.on_screen: Transfer to account → AEPS-supported access.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: घर के बिजली, mobile और gas bills के लिए अलग-अलग व्यवस्था क्यों ढूँढें? मानिए बिजली के ₹600 बाकी हैं; परिवार common payment channel पर जुड़े बिजली provider को चुनता है और ₹600 देता है।
beats.on_screen: Select participating electricity biller; pay ₹600.

beats.say: Payment सफल settle होने पर bill paid दर्ज होता है, और अब उस bill का कुछ बाकी नहीं है। अलग service provider और payment channel ने एक common व्यवस्था में काम किया।
beats.on_screen: Successful settlement → ₹600 bill marked paid; outstanding ₹0.

beats.say: यह Bharat Bill Payment System, BBPS है: bills भरने का single interoperable platform। Interoperable यानी जुड़े payment रास्ते और billers साथ काम कर सकें, जैसे common counter पर अलग सेवाओं के bills; बिजली, mobile, gas और insurance इसके उदाहरण हैं।
beats.on_screen: Four bill types converge on one interoperable platform.

beats.say: लेकिन कोई भी biller दुनिया में कहीं भी हो, वह अपने-आप शामिल नहीं होता। और Bank Mitra से cash निकालना bill aggregation नहीं है; AEPS को BBPS मत समझिए।
beats.on_screen: Participating billers only; cash withdrawal contrasted with bill payment.
beats.source: RBI, Bharat Bill Payment System Directions, 2024

beats.say: BBPS का पहचान वाला शब्द है bill payment: अलग जुड़े billers, एक common व्यवस्था। घर के कई bills साथ दिखें, तो इसी काम को पहचानिए।
beats.on_screen: BBPS → interoperable bill payments.

beats.say: इन दोनों services के ऊपर कौन-सी संस्था जोड़ेंगे? NPCI दोनों को manage करने वाली संस्था है। AEPS का पूरा नाम Aadhaar Enabled Payment System है; Enabled यानी Aadhaar की मदद से banking का रास्ता खुलता है।
beats.on_screen: NPCI branches into AEPS and BBPS; expand AEPS.

beats.say: एक संस्था से जुड़े होने पर भी काम अलग हैं: AEPS में पहचान के जरिए assisted banking; BBPS में common bill payment। संस्था की matching सही रखिए, function को मत मिलाइए।
beats.on_screen: Common institution; distinct functions.

beats.say: अब payment चुनते समय पूछिए: कितनी रकम, कितनी जल्दी, किसको, और किस रास्ते से? Limits की conditions और fee की दिशा जाँचिए; banking access और bill payment को अलग पहचानिए। यही comparison को सही application बनाता है।
beats.on_screen: Decision checklist: amount → urgency → recipient → channel → conditions and fees.

replace_beats.say: किराया, बड़ी urgent payment और बिजली का bill—क्या तीनों के लिए एक ही रास्ता चुनेंगे?
replace_beats.on_screen: Rent, supplier payment and electricity bill.

replace_beats.say: Meena के ₹10000 में से ₹2000 किराया जाने पर ₹8000 बचेंगे। मकान मालिक के ₹1000 में किराया जुड़कर ₹3000 होंगे। बीच में processing कैसे होगी?
replace_beats.on_screen: Jaipur: customer-credit outcome separate from processing.

replace_beats.say: मानिए 10:00 का round खत्म हुआ। Meena ने 10:05 पर ₹2000, Ravi ने 10:12 पर आटे के ₹3000 और Saira ने 10:22 पर fee के ₹1000 भेजने को कहा।
replace_beats.on_screen: Three timestamped instructions form a queue.

replace_beats.say: तीनों अगले 10:30 round के लिए eligible मानिए। ₹6000 के instructions साथ process हुए: यही NEFT batching, यानी आधे घंटे के समूह में processing है। यह ठीक 10:30 पर credit की guarantee नहीं है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Batch processing precedes beneficiary credit; no credit timestamp promised.

replace_beats.say: अब Kavita को steel के ₹300000 Arjun को देने हैं। उनके Bank A में ₹500000, Arjun के Bank B में ₹100000 हैं। Instruction सही और settlement funds पूरे मानिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Fictional Jaipur businesses; separate customer and settlement ledgers.

replace_beats.say: RBI में Bank A से पूरे ₹300000 Bank B को अलग settle होते हैं। Customer credit के बाद Kavita के ₹200000 बचते हैं और Arjun के पास ₹400000 होते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Full-value settlement followed by customer credit; charges ignored.

replace_beats.say: बाद में Arjun पुराने cancelled order के ₹200000 लौटाते हैं। यह अलग पूरा settlement है; उनके ₹200000 बचते हैं, Kavita के ₹400000 होते हैं। सिर्फ ₹100000 का अंतर नहीं भेजा गया।
replace_beats.on_screen: Separate reverse payment; never replace both arrows with net difference.

replace_beats.say: यह RTGS है: real-time यानी batch का इंतजार नहीं; gross यानी पूरी रकम का अलग settlement। यह 24×7 उपलब्ध है, इसलिए बड़ी urgent payment में उपयोगी है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Timing versus individual full-value settlement.

replace_beats.say: गलत instruction या कम funds हों, तो successful settlement नहीं मानेंगे; instant हमेशा सफलता की guarantee नहीं है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Validity and funds checks.

replace_beats.say: किराए के instructions साथ process हुए; steel payment अलग पूरा settle हुआ। फिर customer credit हुआ।
replace_beats.on_screen: Replay both processing paths.
replace_beats.source: RBI, NEFT and RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

replace_beats.say: याद रखिए: NEFT में half-hourly batches; RTGS में हर payment का अलग पूरा settlement होता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Batch versus individual full-value settlement.

replace_beats.say: रविवार रात घर पैसे भेजने हों? NEFT 24×7, यानी सातों दिन खुला है और free of cost है। घर का खर्च भेजना इसका regular-transfer उपयोग समझाता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Weekend household transfer; availability, cost and use shown separately.

replace_beats.say: बड़े supplier payment के लिए RTGS का उपयोग होता है। RBI इसे सीधे चलाता है; sender fee ₹50 तक लेने की अनुमति है, हर बार ₹50 जरूरी नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: High-value use; RBI operator; sender fee ceiling, not flat compulsory charge.

replace_beats.say: रात में परिवार को तुरंत पैसे चाहिए? IMPS immediate और round the clock है। Bank app, website या ATM इसके दरवाजे हैं; दरवाजा और payment system अलग हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Night-time family need; phone, website and ATM access.

replace_beats.say: NEFT में आम तौर पर ₹5 lakh तक और bank-wise limit की बात है, fixed system ceiling नहीं। IMPS में ₹1–₹5 lakh का range मिलता है; minimum की दूसरी wording ‘No minimum’ है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Separate typical use, bank limits and system ceiling; preserve both IMPS minimum formulations.

replace_beats.say: ‘आम तौर पर’ का मतलब ‘सिर्फ’ नहीं है। RTGS की ₹2 lakh minimum बड़ी रकम वाला उपयोग समझाती है; fee में sender और ‘तक’ पकड़िए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Typical use ≠ exclusive use; minimum versus fee ceiling.

replace_beats.say: इन 4 options में समान क्या है? चारों 24×7, all days खुले हैं; रविवार की availability से अकेले चुनाव नहीं होगा।
replace_beats.on_screen: One seven-day clock spans all four columns.

replace_beats.say: NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer है; RTGS, Real-Time Gross Settlement है। IMPS, Immediate Payment Service और UPI, Unified Payments Interface है। Interface यानी payment से जुड़ने का रास्ता, जैसे phone की screen।
replace_beats.on_screen: Expand acronyms; highlight transfer, settlement, immediate and interface.

replace_beats.say: NEFT और RTGS को RBI से, IMPS और UPI को NPCI से जोड़िए। लेकिन network चलाने वाला operator और ऊपर से देखरेख करने वाला regulator अलग हैं; RBI का overarching regulatory role है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Institution matching with operator and regulator roles separated.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

replace_beats.say: NEFT batch में है, इसलिए अगला round आने तक धीमा पड़ सकता है। RTGS real-time gross है; IMPS और UPI भी real-time बताए जाते हैं। आखिरी तीनों की speed instant है; RTGS का जोर high-value पर है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Waiting at a batch gate versus immediate processing.

replace_beats.say: RTGS की minimum ₹2 lakh है; ₹50000 उस दरवाजे से नहीं गुजरेंगे। NEFT, IMPS और UPI की minimum row में ‘No minimum’ है।
replace_beats.on_screen: RTGS entry gate at ₹2 lakh; no minimum in other columns.

replace_beats.say: NEFT की fixed maximum नहीं; RTGS की upper limit नहीं। IMPS में ₹5 lakh, bank-wise फर्क के साथ है। UPI में ₹1 lakh default और Person-to-Merchant के लिए ₹10 lakh है; इसे conditions वाला दरवाजा समझिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Attach bank and category-condition tags to limits; no universal merchant entitlement.

replace_beats.say: NEFT regular, RTGS बड़ी urgent और IMPS रोजमर्रा की urgent payment के लिए है। UPI mobile-based peer-to-peer, जैसे दोस्त को पैसे, और merchant, जैसे दुकान को payment के लिए है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Match household, supplier, urgent family and shop payments.

replace_beats.say: NEFT और RTGS के रास्ते internet तथा mobile banking हैं; IMPS में ATM भी है। UPI में GPay, PhonePe जैसे apps हैं—सामने का रास्ता, पीछे का system नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Access-channel icons connected to underlying systems.

replace_beats.say: Batch का इंतजार समझाता है कि availability और speed अलग क्यों हैं। Gross का मतलब बड़ी रकम नहीं, अलग पूरा settlement है; IMPS-UPI का instant अनुभव पूरा interbank हिसाब नहीं बताता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Availability ≠ speed; gross ≠ high-value; user experience ≠ full settlement mechanism.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

replace_beats.say: ‘हर merchant payment ₹10 lakh तक’ गलत है: eligible category और लागू conditions चाहिए, सिर्फ merchant QR नहीं। Bank की limit भी पूरे system की limit नहीं है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Reject universal merchant entitlement; retain eligibility conditions.
replace_beats.source: NPCI, UPI, Enhancement of Transaction Limits for Certain Categories, 2025

replace_beats.say: इस table को काम, settlement, speed, limits और channel से पढ़िए। खास trap: 24×7 मतलब instant नहीं; RTGS की ₹2 lakh minimum है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Qualified comparison table, including institutional matching.

replace_beats.say: Branch दूर हो तो पैसे कैसे निकालेंगे? गाँव के ग्राहक के खाते में ₹1000 हैं; पास के banking counter से उसे ₹500 चाहिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Distant branch and nearby assisted counter.

replace_beats.say: वह Aadhaar और उँगली के निशान से पहचान जाँच करवाता है। सफल authorised withdrawal पर ₹500 मिलते हैं और खाते में ₹500 बचते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Authenticate, authorise, hand over cash and debit account.

replace_beats.say: Biometrics यानी शरीर की पहचान, जैसे उँगली का निशान। Bank Mitra bank की सेवा पास लाता है; उसके जरिए authentication और payment, banking से दूर व्यक्ति को पहुँच देते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Identity verification and assisted banking are separate functions.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

replace_beats.say: पहचान की जाँच असफल हो, तो इस उदाहरण में withdrawal पूरा नहीं मानेंगे।
replace_beats.on_screen: Failed authentication stops the illustrated path.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

replace_beats.say: Request आई, पहचान जाँची, अनुमति मिली, फिर पैसे निकले; पास का counter दूरी घटाता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Request → authenticate → authorise → withdraw.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

replace_beats.say: Aadhaar, biometrics और Bank Mitra मिलकर banking की पहुँच देते हैं; यही financial inclusion वाला काम है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Identity plus assisted access supports inclusion.

replace_beats.say: सरकारी मदद खाते में हो, पर इस्तेमाल न हो पाए तो? मानिए पहले ₹0 थे; subsidy के ₹500 आने पर ₹500 हुए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Government credits ₹500 to beneficiary account.

replace_beats.say: व्यक्ति Bank Mitra पर Aadhaar-biometric जाँच से पैसे तक पहुँचता है। यही AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को सहारा देना है: आई मदद इस्तेमाल हो सके।
replace_beats.on_screen: Account credit first; assisted access second.

replace_beats.say: पहले सरकार account में benefit देती है; फिर पास की banking access उसे इस्तेमाल करने देती है। दोनों अलग कड़ियाँ हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Delivery → account → access → usable benefit.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

replace_beats.say: Subsidies को grassroots तक पहुँचाने में यही भूमिका है: गाँव के व्यक्ति और खाते के बीच रास्ता खोलना।
replace_beats.on_screen: Local access bridge to credited subsidy.

replace_beats.say: लेकिन banking access मिलना subsidy की eligibility तय नहीं करता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Access ≠ eligibility decision.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

replace_beats.say: पहले benefit खाते में आता है; AEPS उसे इस्तेमाल करने की पहुँच में मदद करता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Benefit delivery followed by AEPS-supported access.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

replace_beats.say: अलग bills के लिए अलग व्यवस्था क्यों ढूँढें? परिवार common channel पर जुड़े बिजली provider को चुनकर बाकी ₹600 भरता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Select participating electricity biller and pay ₹600.

replace_beats.say: सफल settlement पर bill paid होता है; अब ₹0 बाकी हैं। Channel और biller ने साथ काम किया।
replace_beats.on_screen: Successful settlement; bill outstanding ₹0.

replace_beats.say: यह Bharat Bill Payment System, BBPS है: single interoperable platform। यानी जुड़े रास्ते साथ काम करें, जैसे common counter पर बिजली, mobile, gas और insurance bills भरना।
replace_beats.on_screen: Four bill types converge through participating channels and billers.

replace_beats.say: हर biller अपने-आप शामिल नहीं होता। और Bank Mitra से cash निकालना bill payment नहीं है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Participation required; cash withdrawal is not bill payment.
replace_beats.source: RBI, Bharat Bill Payment System Directions, 2024

replace_beats.say: BBPS में अलग जुड़े billers के bills एक common व्यवस्था से भरते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: BBPS → interoperable bill payment.

replace_beats.say: इन दोनों को कौन manage करता है? NPCI दोनों को manage करता है। AEPS, Aadhaar Enabled Payment System है; Enabled यानी Aadhaar की मदद से banking का रास्ता खुलना।
replace_beats.on_screen: Expand AEPS; NPCI branches to AEPS and BBPS.

replace_beats.say: Manager एक है, काम अलग: AEPS assisted banking देता है, BBPS bills भरने का common रास्ता देता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Shared institutional association; different functions.

replace_beats.say: चुनते समय रकम, urgency, recipient, channel और conditions जाँचिए। Fee कौन देगा, यह भी देखिए; banking access और bill payment अलग रखिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Payment-choice checklist.

beats.say: किराया, बड़ी urgent payment और बिजली का bill—क्या तीनों के लिए एक ही रास्ता चुनेंगे?
beats.on_screen: Rent, supplier payment and electricity bill.

beats.say: Meena के ₹10000 में से ₹2000 किराया जाने पर ₹8000 बचेंगे। मकान मालिक के ₹1000 में किराया जुड़कर ₹3000 होंगे। बीच में processing कैसे होगी?
beats.on_screen: Jaipur: customer-credit outcome separate from processing.

beats.say: मानिए 10:00 का round खत्म हुआ। Meena ने 10:05 पर ₹2000, Ravi ने 10:12 पर आटे के ₹3000 और Saira ने 10:22 पर fee के ₹1000 भेजने को कहा।
beats.on_screen: Three timestamped instructions form a queue.

beats.say: तीनों अगले 10:30 round के लिए eligible मानिए। ₹6000 के instructions साथ process हुए: यही NEFT batching, यानी आधे घंटे के समूह में processing है। यह ठीक 10:30 पर credit की guarantee नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Batch processing precedes beneficiary credit; no credit timestamp promised.
beats.source: RBI, NEFT Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: अब Kavita को steel के ₹300000 Arjun को देने हैं। उनके Bank A में ₹500000, Arjun के Bank B में ₹100000 हैं। Instruction सही और settlement funds पूरे मानिए।
beats.on_screen: Fictional Jaipur businesses; separate customer and settlement ledgers.

beats.say: RBI में Bank A से पूरे ₹300000 Bank B को अलग settle होते हैं। Customer credit के बाद Kavita के ₹200000 बचते हैं और Arjun के पास ₹400000 होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Full-value settlement followed by customer credit; charges ignored.

beats.say: बाद में Arjun पुराने cancelled order के ₹200000 लौटाते हैं। यह अलग पूरा settlement है; उनके ₹200000 बचते हैं, Kavita के ₹400000 होते हैं। सिर्फ ₹100000 का अंतर नहीं भेजा गया।
beats.on_screen: Separate reverse payment; never replace both arrows with net difference.

beats.say: यह RTGS है: real-time यानी batch का इंतजार नहीं; gross यानी पूरी रकम का अलग settlement। यह 24×7 उपलब्ध है, इसलिए बड़ी urgent payment में उपयोगी है।
beats.on_screen: Timing versus individual full-value settlement.
beats.source: RBI, RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: गलत instruction या कम funds हों, तो successful settlement नहीं मानेंगे; instant हमेशा सफलता की guarantee नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Validity and funds checks.
beats.source: RBI, RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: किराए के instructions साथ process हुए; steel payment अलग पूरा settle हुआ। फिर customer credit हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Replay both processing paths.
beats.source: RBI, NEFT and RTGS Frequently Asked Questions, 2024

beats.say: याद रखिए: NEFT में half-hourly batches; RTGS में हर payment का अलग पूरा settlement होता है।
beats.on_screen: Batch versus individual full-value settlement.

beats.say: रविवार रात घर पैसे भेजने हों? NEFT 24×7, यानी सातों दिन खुला है और free of cost है। घर का खर्च भेजना इसका regular-transfer उपयोग समझाता है।
beats.on_screen: Weekend household transfer; availability, cost and use shown separately.

beats.say: बड़े supplier payment के लिए RTGS का उपयोग होता है। RBI इसे सीधे चलाता है; sender fee ₹50 तक लेने की अनुमति है, हर बार ₹50 जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: High-value use; RBI operator; sender fee ceiling, not flat compulsory charge.

beats.say: रात में परिवार को तुरंत पैसे चाहिए? IMPS immediate और round the clock है। Bank app, website या ATM इसके दरवाजे हैं; दरवाजा और payment system अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Night-time family need; phone, website and ATM access.

beats.say: NEFT में आम तौर पर ₹5 lakh तक और bank-wise limit की बात है, fixed system ceiling नहीं। IMPS में ₹1–₹5 lakh का range मिलता है; minimum की दूसरी wording ‘No minimum’ है।
beats.on_screen: Separate typical use, bank limits and system ceiling; preserve both IMPS minimum formulations.

beats.say: ‘आम तौर पर’ का मतलब ‘सिर्फ’ नहीं है। RTGS की ₹2 lakh minimum बड़ी रकम वाला उपयोग समझाती है; fee में sender और ‘तक’ पकड़िए।
beats.on_screen: Typical use ≠ exclusive use; minimum versus fee ceiling.

beats.say: इन 4 options में समान क्या है? चारों 24×7, all days खुले हैं; रविवार की availability से अकेले चुनाव नहीं होगा।
beats.on_screen: One seven-day clock spans all four columns.

beats.say: NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer है; RTGS, Real-Time Gross Settlement है। IMPS, Immediate Payment Service और UPI, Unified Payments Interface है। Interface यानी payment से जुड़ने का रास्ता, जैसे phone की screen।
beats.on_screen: Expand acronyms; highlight transfer, settlement, immediate and interface.

beats.say: NEFT और RTGS को RBI से, IMPS और UPI को NPCI से जोड़िए। लेकिन network चलाने वाला operator और ऊपर से देखरेख करने वाला regulator अलग हैं; RBI का overarching regulatory role है।
beats.on_screen: Institution matching with operator and regulator roles separated.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

beats.say: NEFT batch में है, इसलिए अगला round आने तक धीमा पड़ सकता है। RTGS real-time gross है; IMPS और UPI भी real-time बताए जाते हैं। आखिरी तीनों की speed instant है; RTGS का जोर high-value पर है।
beats.on_screen: Waiting at a batch gate versus immediate processing.

beats.say: RTGS की minimum ₹2 lakh है; ₹50000 उस दरवाजे से नहीं गुजरेंगे। NEFT, IMPS और UPI की minimum row में ‘No minimum’ है।
beats.on_screen: RTGS entry gate at ₹2 lakh; no minimum in other columns.

beats.say: NEFT की fixed maximum नहीं; RTGS की upper limit नहीं। IMPS में ₹5 lakh, bank-wise फर्क के साथ है। UPI में ₹1 lakh default और Person-to-Merchant के लिए ₹10 lakh है; इसे conditions वाला दरवाजा समझिए।
beats.on_screen: Attach bank and category-condition tags to limits; no universal merchant entitlement.

beats.say: NEFT regular, RTGS बड़ी urgent और IMPS रोजमर्रा की urgent payment के लिए है। UPI mobile-based peer-to-peer, जैसे दोस्त को पैसे, और merchant, जैसे दुकान को payment के लिए है।
beats.on_screen: Match household, supplier, urgent family and shop payments.

beats.say: NEFT और RTGS के रास्ते internet तथा mobile banking हैं; IMPS में ATM भी है। UPI में GPay, PhonePe जैसे apps हैं—सामने का रास्ता, पीछे का system नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Access-channel icons connected to underlying systems.

beats.say: Batch का इंतजार समझाता है कि availability और speed अलग क्यों हैं। Gross का मतलब बड़ी रकम नहीं, अलग पूरा settlement है; IMPS-UPI का instant अनुभव पूरा interbank हिसाब नहीं बताता।
beats.on_screen: Availability ≠ speed; gross ≠ high-value; user experience ≠ full settlement mechanism.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

beats.say: ‘हर merchant payment ₹10 lakh तक’ गलत है: eligible category और लागू conditions चाहिए, सिर्फ merchant QR नहीं। Bank की limit भी पूरे system की limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Reject universal merchant entitlement; retain eligibility conditions.
beats.source: NPCI, UPI, Enhancement of Transaction Limits for Certain Categories, 2025

beats.say: इस table को काम, settlement, speed, limits और channel से पढ़िए। खास trap: 24×7 मतलब instant नहीं; RTGS की ₹2 lakh minimum है।
beats.on_screen: Qualified comparison table, including institutional matching.

beats.say: Branch दूर हो तो पैसे कैसे निकालेंगे? गाँव के ग्राहक के खाते में ₹1000 हैं; पास के banking counter से उसे ₹500 चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Distant branch and nearby assisted counter.

beats.say: वह Aadhaar और उँगली के निशान से पहचान जाँच करवाता है। सफल authorised withdrawal पर ₹500 मिलते हैं और खाते में ₹500 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Authenticate, authorise, hand over cash and debit account.

beats.say: Biometrics यानी शरीर की पहचान, जैसे उँगली का निशान। Bank Mitra bank की सेवा पास लाता है; उसके जरिए authentication और payment, banking से दूर व्यक्ति को पहुँच देते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Identity verification and assisted banking are separate functions.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: पहचान की जाँच असफल हो, तो इस उदाहरण में withdrawal पूरा नहीं मानेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Failed authentication stops the illustrated path.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems

beats.say: Request आई, पहचान जाँची, अनुमति मिली, फिर पैसे निकले; पास का counter दूरी घटाता है।
beats.on_screen: Request → authenticate → authorise → withdraw.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: Aadhaar, biometrics और Bank Mitra मिलकर banking की पहुँच देते हैं; यही financial inclusion वाला काम है।
beats.on_screen: Identity plus assisted access supports inclusion.

beats.say: सरकारी मदद खाते में हो, पर इस्तेमाल न हो पाए तो? मानिए पहले ₹0 थे; subsidy के ₹500 आने पर ₹500 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Government credits ₹500 to beneficiary account.

beats.say: व्यक्ति Bank Mitra पर Aadhaar-biometric जाँच से पैसे तक पहुँचता है। यही AEPS का Direct Benefits Transfer को सहारा देना है: आई मदद इस्तेमाल हो सके।
beats.on_screen: Account credit first; assisted access second.

beats.say: पहले सरकार account में benefit देती है; फिर पास की banking access उसे इस्तेमाल करने देती है। दोनों अलग कड़ियाँ हैं।
beats.on_screen: Delivery → account → access → usable benefit.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: Subsidies को grassroots तक पहुँचाने में यही भूमिका है: गाँव के व्यक्ति और खाते के बीच रास्ता खोलना।
beats.on_screen: Local access bridge to credited subsidy.

beats.say: लेकिन banking access मिलना subsidy की eligibility तय नहीं करता।
beats.on_screen: Access ≠ eligibility decision.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: पहले benefit खाते में आता है; AEPS उसे इस्तेमाल करने की पहुँच में मदद करता है।
beats.on_screen: Benefit delivery followed by AEPS-supported access.
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Financial Inclusion and Development

beats.say: अलग bills के लिए अलग व्यवस्था क्यों ढूँढें? परिवार common channel पर जुड़े बिजली provider को चुनकर बाकी ₹600 भरता है।
beats.on_screen: Select participating electricity biller and pay ₹600.

beats.say: सफल settlement पर bill paid होता है; अब ₹0 बाकी हैं। Channel और biller ने साथ काम किया।
beats.on_screen: Successful settlement; bill outstanding ₹0.

beats.say: यह Bharat Bill Payment System, BBPS है: single interoperable platform। यानी जुड़े रास्ते साथ काम करें, जैसे common counter पर बिजली, mobile, gas और insurance bills भरना।
beats.on_screen: Four bill types converge through participating channels and billers.

beats.say: हर biller अपने-आप शामिल नहीं होता। और Bank Mitra से cash निकालना bill payment नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Participation required; cash withdrawal is not bill payment.
beats.source: RBI, Bharat Bill Payment System Directions, 2024

beats.say: BBPS में अलग जुड़े billers के bills एक common व्यवस्था से भरते हैं।
beats.on_screen: BBPS → interoperable bill payment.

beats.say: इन दोनों को कौन manage करता है? NPCI दोनों को manage करता है। AEPS, Aadhaar Enabled Payment System है; Enabled यानी Aadhaar की मदद से banking का रास्ता खुलना।
beats.on_screen: Expand AEPS; NPCI branches to AEPS and BBPS.

beats.say: उन्हें अपने दोनों counters से जोड़िए: एक पर Aadhaar से banking मिली, दूसरे पर बिजली का bill भरा।
beats.on_screen: NPCI above the two familiar service counters.

beats.say: Manager एक है, काम अलग: AEPS assisted banking देता है, BBPS bills भरने का common रास्ता देता है।
beats.on_screen: Shared institutional association; different functions.

beats.say: चुनते समय रकम, urgency, recipient, channel और conditions जाँचिए। Fee कौन देगा, यह भी देखिए; banking access और bill payment अलग रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment-choice checklist.
